title: A retro boarding pass scanner
summary: Drag the pass through a beige reader: too fast is an error, steady gets you in.
brief: Build a beige boarding pass scanner that reads a pass as I drag it through the slot. Reject a fast swipe with a red light and grant access on a steady swipe.

prompts.text:
Build a web page with a vintage boarding pass floating over a beige plastic scanner. On a 960 × 540 warm off-white field centre a 445 × 210 ticket at y=20 and a 445 × 146 reader at y=310. No surrounding UI. Give the reader two banks of vents, a recessed slot, deep bevels, a central black dot-matrix screen and a round status lamp at right. Under it: “Swipe boarding pass to enter”.
Make the pass feel like printed paper, not an app card. Use pale grey-white stock, fine grain, barely lavender map-like veins in the corners, rounded edges, a soft shadow and a moving sheen. The main part takes three quarters of the width; the stub occupies the last quarter. Add short violet diagonal stripes at the left edge. Across the narrow header put a tiny boxed globe of your own design, ATU AIR, a hairline separator, a spaced micro-tagline and a small faded red round stamp with invented microlettering. Keep the printing quiet and airy, in typewriter mono: tiny violet labels, dark values. Passenger SAM REYES at left, flight and date to the right; below those put SYD and KIX with tiny city lines. At actual size the name and airport codes are only 13–15 px, NOT big headlines. Below: a fine rounded five-cell strip (gate, boarding, seat, class, sequence), with a tiny footnote in each cell; beside it a faint circular globe seal. Follow with a tiny plane and two notice lines, then a wide, shallow, dense black 2D barcode with microprint below. On the perforated stub repeat the miniature globe header and flight fields, route with a plane, seat, class and sequence, rotated fine print and a little outlined tag. Invent the fine print and marks. Use a fixed 445 × 210 print coordinate system. At x=16 put a 14 px violet globe box, a 6 px header wordmark and tiny tagline, no header rule; the red inspection stamp near x=286 is only 7 px across. Passenger occupies the left half of the main part; keep the area below the name mostly blank except a tiny occupation line and pale lavender branching marbling. Put FROM and TO directly under FLIGHT and DATE in the right half at x=185 and 250, not under the name. Keep the five-cell outline hairline and reserve just the bottom 14 px for black barcode modules with short side fences. Fine ink should be blue-violet rather than brown. Set the stub division at x=340; repeat the minuscule globe and light header there. Below that stub header print PASSENGER and SAM REYES, then FLIGHT and DATE together, FROM and TO with a small plane, seat and class, sequence, and the tag. Check that SAM REYES actually appears twice. Use dark semibold compact mono for the name and codes; pale violet tiny caps for labels; make the seal about 40 px across. Aim for muted grey paper rather than bright white, and a pinkish ivory backdrop. Set the idle tilt slightly clockwise, not counter-clockwise. Put the paper behind the top AND front of the scanner while feeding it in, leaving its top half visible. Use a plain beige reader like a 1980s peripheral with no text other than its screen and caption. Idle is stationary; the slight paper sheen follows the tilt, not an automatic repeating animation. The three LED states need a visible coloured halo.
Let me grab the slightly tilted pass anywhere. Make held paper trail the pointer with a soft damped spring. As I sweep left or right and reverse, visibly roll it a few degrees and pitch/yaw it in perspective; quick pulls bend it further and a pause lets it settle. Let me lift it back out. Lower it behind the reader front and flatten it in the slot: amber READING as I swipe sideways, a fast half-second swipe gives red ERROR and a retry, a steady two-second swipe gives green SUCCESS and “Access granted”. Hold, fly the pass away, then reset exactly to idle READY. Use local HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Build it in a new folder inside the current project folder, open it in the browser when done, check that it works, and ask me before installing or loading anything.

action.label: Build the pass scanner in Atu

made.alt: A paper boarding pass tilts as the cursor changes direction, then straightens behind a beige scanner. The fast swipe shows ERROR. A steady swipe shows SUCCESS before the pass flies away and the reader resets.
made.caption: A fast swipe fails. A steady swipe turns the light green and grants access.
